llm.summary: The skill is mostly aligned with its stated Dataify collection purpose, but it needs review because it handles personal-profile collection, long-lived API tokens, implicit invocation, and an unreviewed helper import.

dimensions.detail: Network access to Dataify and DATAIFY_API_TOKEN use are purpose-aligned, but the skill does not declare tight permission boundaries and may send Facebook profile URLs and use account credits without a clear confirmation gate.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: There is no install-time script or hidden installer, but the runtime script prepends a sibling directory outside the reviewed package to sys.path and imports task_runtime from there.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The English instructions include safer token handling, but the Chinese instructions also tell the agent to accept or request an API token in conversation, and the agent manifest allows implicit invocation for an external collection workflow.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill does not create services, scheduled tasks, or silently persist tokens; it does instruct users how to set a persistent environment variable and then reuses that saved token.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifacts consistently describe submitting Facebook personal profile URLs to Dataify, monitoring the task, and returning results; that capability is coherent with the stated purpose but is privacy- and credit-impacting.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use this only if you intend to send Facebook profile URLs to Dataify and potentially spend account credits. Configure DATAIFY_API_TOKEN through an environment variable or secret manager, do not paste the token into chat, and only use the default wait/result retrieval flow if you trust the separate dataify-task-operations helper available in the runtime environment.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Environment token use and outbound Dataify requests are necessary for the stated integration, but missing explicit permission boundaries remains a review concern.
[EA2] expected: Using a saved token without re-prompting and applying defaults is disclosed; the concern is limited to confirmation around credit- and privacy-impacting collection, not destructive local behavior.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The localized file contains contradictory dashboard and token guidance, which weakens consistent operator behavior but does not show deception by itself.
[SQP-3] unexpected: The mixed-language account policy is a quality and clarity issue; it did not materially drive the verdict beyond the token-handling inconsistency.
[SQP-1] expected: Implicit invocation is explicitly enabled and aligned with the collection purpose, but it is under-scoped for a third-party personal-data collection action.
[SDI-1] expected: Post-submission monitoring and result retrieval are disclosed in the English skill and agent prompt, so this was downgraded as expected behavior.
[T08] unexpected: The script imports a task_runtime module from a sibling directory outside the inspected artifact and passes it the API token during result monitoring.
[T09] unexpected: The Chinese instructions and script error text can lead users to provide a long-lived API token in chat, conflicting with the later no-paste rule.
